entries.proposition: Maturation-dependent role of the channel: low-threshold calcium spikes are frequent in immature dentate granule cells that fire one action potential (15 of 19 wild-type), and the proportion falls to 3 of 18 in Cav3.2 knockout (Fisher p = 0.0002). The spike is blocked by a pan-T-type blocker in wild-type cells and is insensitive to TTX. The channel contributes an excitability feature specific to immature cells.
entries.snippet: However, the overall proportion of immature GCs with LTCS was significantly reduced (KO n = 3/18 cells; Fisher's exact test, p = 0.0002; Fig. 2B).
entries.anchor: Results, Loss of T-type calcium channels impairs LTCS in immature GCs

entries.proposition: Direction of the knockout effect is not uniform: in regular-spiking intermediate and mature granule cells loss of Cav3.2 increases excitability (shorter intervals between spikes; higher average firing frequency in mature cells), the opposite of what blocking a depolarising channel would predict if only the immature effect were considered. The authors suggest coupling to a calcium-activated potassium channel without testing it.
entries.snippet: Overall, these results indicate that loss of Cav3.2 channels in regular spiking GCs increases excitability.
entries.anchor: Results, Loss of Cav3.2 increases GC excitability in regular spiking cells

entries.proposition: The authors write that, despite a strong phenotype, their results indicate that the effects of the Cav3.2 knockout on granule-cell intrinsic excitability are relatively subtle.
entries.snippet: Despite this strong phenotype, our results indicate that the effects of Cav3.2 KO on GC intrinsic excitability are relatively subtle.

entries.proposition: Compensation limit: low-threshold spikes remain in about 17 percent of knockout immature cells, and the authors list Cav3.1, Cav3.3 and Cav2.3 as candidates, or compensation, so even a genetic loss of one subtype does not remove the current; a pharmacological block of 'T-type' is a different perturbation from a Cav3.2 null.
entries.snippet: indicating that Cav3.2 channels may not solely underlie LTCS.
